scene: A captain wants a sea-loan on his hull and cargo: you carry the risk of the sea, he pays a third over if he returns. He is sailing for Alexandria in the wrong month.

choices.label: Lend at the sea-rate
choices.resultText: He returns, late, with papyrus and a story about a waterspout. A third over, and a captain who will borrow from you first, always.

choices.label: Refuse; the sea is not a partner
choices.resultText: He borrows from a Punic factor. He returns. The factor's third is the factor's.

scene: The market wardens are inspecting weights in the agora. Your steward's scale is honest; your warehouse scale has been generous to you for a year.

choices.label: Fix the warehouse scale before they reach it
choices.resultText: The scale is honest by the time the wardens arrive. It is honest afterward too, which costs you the year's generosity.

choices.label: Show them the scale and pay the fine
choices.resultText: The wardens, who expected to find it, are startled to be shown it. The fine is light. The story is heavy, in your favor.

scene: An Alexandrian factor offers a standing contract for papyrus at a price that only makes sense if he is being paid to undercut Rhodes.

choices.label: Sign it and ask no questions
choices.resultText: Papyrus by the bale, cheap, for two years. Then a Rhodian visits and asks you, politely, whose contract you signed.

choices.label: Ask the questions first
choices.resultText: Ptolemy's treasury is behind it, and Rhodes knows. You sign for one year, at a rate that will not be remembered against you.

scene: Your partner at Emporion has stopped writing. A captain says he has taken an Iberian wife and a new counting-house, with your share of the stock.

choices.label: Sail to Emporion and see for yourself
choices.resultText: He has taken a wife, a counting-house, and your share, and is astonished to be asked about it. You leave with the share and a new partner, the wife's brother.

choices.label: Write to Emporion's magistrates
choices.resultText: The magistrates recover half. The other half is a lesson about partners and distance.

scene: Ligurian salt-boilers offer a season's salt for wine, direct, cutting out the Massaliote salt-factor who has cornered the trade.

choices.label: Deal direct
choices.resultText: Salt for wine at the beach, in two languages. The salt-factor complains to the council. The council, which likes cheap salt, does nothing.

choices.label: Buy from the factor, as custom is
choices.resultText: Salt at the factor's price. Custom kept. The Ligurians sell their salt to a Rhodian who does not care about custom.

scene: Your clerk's sums are wrong every month by a little, always in his favor. He is also the only man alive who understands your ledgers.

choices.label: Confront him and dock the difference
choices.resultText: He pays it back, ashamed, and stays. The ledgers are honest for a year, and then you check again.

choices.label: Train a second clerk and dismiss him
choices.resultText: Two clerks who check each other, and a former clerk telling the harbor you are ungrateful. The sums are right.

scene: Your Ilergetae trading partner invites you to his daughter's wedding: a week's sail, a week's feast, and the whole tribe's trade to think about.

choices.label: Go, with a gift worth the voyage
choices.resultText: A week of Iberian beer and songs about horses. His sons now sell only to you. His daughter's husband sells to you too.

choices.label: Send a gift and your apologies
choices.resultText: The gift is admired. Your apology is accepted. A Rhodian who went to the wedding is now his sons' second choice.

scene: Your captain is taken by Ligurian pirates off the Stoechades. The ransom is the value of the ship. The ship is still yours.

choices.label: Pay the ransom
choices.resultText: He comes home thin and loyal. Every sailor on the coast knows which trader pays for his men.

choices.label: Refuse; ransoms breed pirates
choices.resultText: He comes home a year later, sold twice, having escaped. He does not sail for you. Nobody who heard the story does either.

scene: Carthage's factor offers credit at half the Greek rate to any Massaliote who will ship through Punic ports. It is not a secret; it is a policy.

choices.label: Take the credit
choices.resultText: Cheap silver and Punic harbors. Your ships are seen at Carthage. The old families see the manifests.

choices.label: Refuse, and say why in the agora
choices.resultText: Your speech about Punic silver is quoted for a season. Your credit is at the Greek rate, which is what a speech costs.

scene: Fire in the harbor warehouses. Yours is next to the one burning, and the dockworkers are asking what it is worth to them to stay.

choices.label: Pay them double and fight it
choices.resultText: Your warehouse stands, scorched. The dockworkers, paid double, remember which trader stayed with them in the smoke.

choices.label: Save the books and let the goods go
choices.resultText: The books are safe; you know exactly what you lost. Your creditors, oddly, respect the exact figure.

scene: Word from the north: the tin route you pioneered is being used by a Rhodian who bought the sailing directions from your old captain.

choices.label: Send two ships and out-trade him
choices.resultText: Your ships arrive first at the tin-beaches with better wine. The Rhodian arrives second and buys your tin at your price.

choices.label: Sell the Rhodian the rest of the directions
choices.resultText: He pays for what he already half-knew. You have the silver and the parts of the route you did not sell.

scene: The Olympiad year. Traders from every Greek city meet at Olympia to trade without tariff. It is a month's sail, and every rival will be there.

choices.label: Go with your best cargo
choices.resultText: Massaliote wine and Ligurian amber, sold under the god's truce to men from Byzantion and Cyrene. Your name is known in cities you will never see.

choices.label: Stay and trade the empty harbor
choices.resultText: The harbor is yours for a month. Prices are excellent. Everyone who went to Olympia comes back with a story you are not in.

scene: The dockworkers have stopped work over a foreman's cruelty. Your cargo is on the quay in the sun, and the foreman is your foreman.

choices.label: Dismiss the foreman and settle
choices.resultText: Work resumes by noon. The new foreman is one of them. Your cargo moves first, always, after this.

choices.label: Hire Gaulish hands to unload
choices.resultText: The cargo moves. The dockworkers return in a week and remember. Your cargo moves last, always, after this.

scene: Your best captain asks for your niece for his son. It would bind him to your house. It would also bind your house to a captain.

choices.label: Agree to the match
choices.resultText: A wedding on the quay. The captain's son is a good boy and the captain now sails as if the ship were his own family's. It is.

choices.label: Decline gently; the house marries up
choices.resultText: He sails for you a year longer, correctly. Then he sails for a Rhodian who married his son to a Rhodian.

scene: A Volcae chief who hates Greeks holds the only road to the Garonne tin. Every trader has tried him. The Ephors ask you to try.

choices.label: Go up and talk
choices.resultText: Three days, a great deal of beer, and a chief who ends by calling you a liar and a friend. The road opens. Every trader in Massalia knows who opened it.

choices.label: Decline; some doors are not for talking through
choices.resultText: A Rhodian tries. He comes back without his cargo and with a very good story about the chief's beer.

scene: A bookseller offers a complete copy of On the Ocean, Pytheas's own account, with the tables. It costs a ship's worth of wine.

choices.label: Buy it and read it twice
choices.resultText: Tides, tin, amber, a sea like a lung. You believe it. Your captains, reading your sailing orders, begin to believe it too.

choices.label: Borrow it for a night and copy the tables
choices.resultText: The tables, in your hand, by dawn. The rest of the book you remember imperfectly, which is how Pytheas is usually remembered.

scene: A glassmaker in Agathe has a kiln and no market. He offers you everything he makes for three years at a fixed price.

choices.label: Sign for three years
choices.resultText: Agathe glass in every Gaulish hill-fort by the second year, at Massaliote prices. The glassmaker's sons work for you.

choices.label: Sign for one year and see
choices.resultText: One good year. Then a Rhodian signs for ten.

scene: The harbor's traders want a guild with a common warehouse and a common enemy: the Rhodians. You are asked to draft the charter.

choices.label: Draft it and take the first chair
choices.resultText: A charter, a warehouse, and a year of chairing men who agree on nothing but Rhodes. The Rhodians, hearing of it, lower their prices.

choices.label: Join and let another man chair
choices.resultText: The guild works, mostly. The chair is blamed for the rest. You share the warehouse and none of the blame.

scene: A potter offers to stamp Chian seals on your Massaliote wine amphorae. Chian wine sells for triple. Chians, occasionally, visit.

choices.label: Stamp them
choices.resultText: Triple, for a season. A Chian visits, tastes, and laughs so loudly the whole quay hears which trader sells Chian.

choices.label: Make your own seal and sell it as what it is
choices.resultText: Your seal on your wine. In three years, Gaulish chiefs ask for the seal by name, and a potter in Agathe offers to counterfeit it.

scene: A Roman quaestor offers a contract to supply the legions in the south with wine and oil, paid in Roman silver on Roman terms.

choices.label: Take it
choices.resultText: Roman silver, paid late and in full. Your ships are known in Ostia. Carthage's factor stops buying your oil.

choices.label: Refuse; Rome's wars are Rome's
choices.resultText: A Rhodian takes it. Rome remembers Rhodes. Your oil sells to Carthage, for now.

scene: The customs officer at the mole suggests your cargo of Punic dye might be recorded as Egyptian, at Egyptian rates, for a consideration.

choices.label: Agree
choices.resultText: Egyptian dye, on paper. The consideration is small. He suggests it again next month, less small.

choices.label: Decline and pay the Punic rate
choices.resultText: Punic dye, at Punic rates. The officer marks you as a man who pays, and does not suggest things to you again. He suggests them to your rivals.

scene: Your chief rival's ship is on the rocks off Olbia. His cargo is yours to buy from the salvagers, cheap, and he is on the beach watching.

choices.label: Buy it cheap
choices.resultText: His amphorae, your prices. He walks home. He does not forget the beach, and neither, in fairness, do you.

choices.label: Buy it back for him at cost and lend him a hull
choices.resultText: He sails home in your hull with his cargo. He is your rival for twenty more years and never once undercuts you in a bad season.

scene: A Gaulish chief offers captives from a raid: Saluvii, thirty of them, at a price that would make the season. The temple registrar's daughter is your clerk.

choices.label: Buy and sell them on
choices.resultText: The season is made. The Saluvii, when they hear which trader bought their cousins, remember. So does your clerk, who stops speaking to you.

choices.label: Refuse; you trade in things
choices.resultText: The chief sells them to a Punic factor. The Saluvii hear which trader refused. It is worth something, later, on a hill road.

scene: The Helvii want wine, a hundred amphorae, delivered upriver. The river is low and the Cavares are between you and the Helvii.

choices.label: Send it under Cavares escort, for a toll
choices.resultText: The Cavares take a tenth and deliver ninety. The Helvii are drunk for a month and ask for two hundred next year.

choices.label: Wait for the spring flood and go alone
choices.resultText: Spring, a full river, no toll. The Helvii drank Volcae beer all winter and are less thirsty.

scene: A sailor in a tavern says the Syracusan grain fleet has been lost in a storm. If true, grain triples by dawn. If false, whoever buys tonight is a fool.

choices.label: Buy every sack in the harbor tonight
choices.resultText: True. Grain triples. You sell at dawn to men who did not drink in that tavern.

choices.label: Send a boat to the islands to check
choices.resultText: True, but by the time your boat returns the price has moved. You buy what is left, at a price that is still good.

scene: Your counting-house clerk, a freedman, asks to marry your steward's daughter. The steward is a citizen and furious.

choices.label: Bless it and give the dowry yourself
choices.resultText: A wedding in the counting-house. The steward sulks and then dances. The clerk's sums, from that day, are the most honest in Massalia.

choices.label: Forbid it; the house has an order
choices.resultText: The clerk leaves for a Rhodian house, and takes the daughter. The steward blames you for both.

scene: A Gaulish trader offers a hoard of amber, old pieces with insects in them, from a grave. He does not say a grave. His hands say it.

choices.label: Buy it
choices.resultText: The insects sell to a Syracusan collector for four times the price. You do not ask about the grave. The grave, presumably, does not ask about you.

choices.label: Refuse; grave-goods are not goods
choices.resultText: He sells it to a Rhodian. The Rhodian's ship is lost off Sardinia. You are not superstitious, and you note it.

scene: The Archons want a trader to go to Rhoda as envoy, to settle a harbor-fee quarrel that has stopped the League's western trade.

choices.label: Go as envoy
choices.resultText: A month of Rhodan magistrates and a fee-schedule everyone hates equally, which is a treaty. Your ships pay it first.

choices.label: Decline; envoys are not paid
choices.resultText: A Kleitos goes and settles it worse. Your ships pay the fee. You did not have to go to Rhoda, which is something.

scene: The city is auctioning the right to collect harbor tax for a year. The winner keeps what he collects above his bid. Your rivals are bidding.

choices.label: Bid, and collect hard
choices.resultText: You win the bid and collect every obol. The harbor pays and hates you for a year. The year is very profitable.

choices.label: Stay out of tax-farming
choices.resultText: A Timon wins and collects hard. The harbor hates him. You trade, and are, by comparison, beloved.

scene: In a gale off Antipolis your captain vowed a silver ship to Artemis if the hull survived. It survived. He wants you to pay for the silver ship.

choices.label: Pay for the vow
choices.resultText: A silver ship, a hand long, in the temple. Every sailor in the harbor knows whose hull it is and whose vow was kept.

choices.label: Tell the captain his vow is his
choices.resultText: He pays for a smaller ship, in bronze. He sails for you another year, and then for a trader who pays for vows.

scene: The customs house audits the harbor's most prominent trader once a decade, and this decade it is you. Ten years of manifests, and a clerk who is enjoying himself.

choices.label: Pay the assessment and be done
choices.resultText: Ten years of small generosities, totaled and doubled. You pay. The clerk thanks you for your cooperation.

choices.label: Contest it in the assembly
choices.resultText: You win half the points and all of the reputation of a man who argues with the customs house. The half you lost still costs.

scene: A winter of ledgers by lamplight and a fever from the harbor. The physician says a month of rest, or a mind that never quite adds as fast again.

choices.label: Rest the month
choices.resultText: A month in bed while your clerks trade badly in your name. You recover. The books do not, for a season.

choices.label: Work through it
choices.resultText: You keep trading. The fever breaks. The sums come slower now, and you check them twice, and sometimes that is not enough.
